facts.statement: verify every claim with web search and repository documents; a claim matching repository documents can still be wrong and externally verifiable claims need an external source
cite a source for each important claim using the citation and linking convention
apply only spelling, grammar, and capitalization fixes directly in place; everything else goes in the audit report
use the Oxford comma in every list of three or more items
use MLA-style title casing for section headers
flag structural problems and statements with ambiguous subjects or referents
propose illustrations and analogies to explain complex concepts
example proposals are 'Bad / Good / Why' blocks with a one-sentence caption under each version
propose a call-out quote for the start of every section, one per section with none skipped, a one-sentence quote distilling the section's central thesis

repetition is acceptable only when the concept is important enough, relevant in each section where it appears, and worded differently each time; evaluate every occurrence against all three criteria separately
any line starting with '> EDITOR:' is a direct request from the author; resolve each one and remove or rewrite the marker line
flag any link not written as [label](url)
flag any multi-line code block with lines longer than 80 characters; the 80-character limit applies to code blocks only, not blockquotes or other preformatted elements
list every source in a '## References' section at the bottom with letter keys in order of first citation, each entry of the form '- **[A]** [Source - Title](url)'
cite inline as '[A](#ref-a)' immediately after the claim it supports; descriptive link text allowed but the anchor target must always be the reference's '#ref-x' anchor
cite multiple sources grouped in one pair of parentheses, comma-separated
never use bare URLs, footnote-style markers, or any other citation format
the report skeleton is numbered sections with lettered items (1. category -> 1.a finding); every finding is exactly one lettered item, never bare bullets or prose paragraphs
include an example or concrete suggestion for each proposed fix
reference locations by describing them or quoting a snippet of surrounding text, never line numbers
report how each '> EDITOR:' directive was resolved

excluded.reason: engagement-without-dilution goal is a rationale, not a testable directive
step ordering (fact-check first, copyedit second) is workflow sequencing, not a separable output-shaping fact
all three gotchas restate Workflow facts already inventoried (direct-edit scope, external verification, repetition)
checklist items restate the body facts already inventoried
